project_specification.project_name: nullius — wire the leakage tripwires into live evaluation (step 10) and run the M1 triage on real campaigns
project_specification.addition_summary:
PRD M1's exit has two halves. - The KS guard confirming that planted nulls are indistinguishable now passes on a real campaign: campaign bb0f1919 on 2026-10-08, KS p=0.45, calibration ok, after the null time-leak fix (0497a90). - "A deliberately leaking signal is caught by every tripwire" cannot pass yet. The tripwires member ships the six probes (features 125–130: time-shuffle, label-permute, seed re-run, window offset, universe subsample, lookback jitter), but orchestrator._evaluate never calls them: perturb_stability is hard-coded None (_evaluate.py ~:479, ~:893), and every node of every real campaign has a NULL perturb_stability. The M1 one-day triage, the perturbation-stability AUC that separates planted nulls from real nodes, therefore cannot run on real data either.
This spec seats step 10 (architecture §6.1: after metrics, before debit_ledger), proves that a leaking signal fails every probe, and makes close-out emit the triage AUC per campaign. Every probe is a pure function of (scores, targets) that the evaluator already holds, so step 10 adds no sandbox runs.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / SQLite at DATABASE_URL (default ~/.local/share/nullius/research.db) / pytest.
existing_context.test_baseline: main at a38fc47: gate command (uv run --all-packages pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile) 1648 passed; orchestrator 477 passed 5 skipped; nulloracle 1378; signal-agent 800; evaluator 569.
existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md. - Null status never leaves the scorer process. Only close-out (which already holds the sidecar) may join perturbation figures to labels. Step 10 runs identically for null and real nodes, against the same target bundle the node is scored on. - Tests pass under pytest-xdist and never touch the network or a credential.
Existing pieces (all in packages/tripwires/src/tripwires/): - time_shuffle.run_time_shuffle_tripwire(scores, targets, *, node_id, seed, level) - label_permute.run_label_permute_tripwire(scores, targets, *, node_id, seed, level) - seed_rerun.run_seed_rerun(scores, targets, *, node_id, ...) - window_offset.run_window_rerun(scores, targets, *, node_id, ...) - subsample.run_subsample_rerun(scores, targets, *, node_id, ...) - lookback.run_lookback_rerun(scores, targets, *, node_id, ...) In all six, scores is {date: {symbol: float}} and targets is {horizon: {date: {symbol: float}}}. Each answers a verdict value whose rejection is a field, never an exception. - stability.record_stability: per-axis figures (feature 129). - node_metric.NodeMetricStore / record_node_metric: writes node.perturb_stability from the lookback verdict (feature 130). It requires the node row to exist. - poison.py: feature 131 poisons a failing node and its subtree. - corpus.py: the planted-leak corpus (feature 133). - triage.py: the AUC over the member's own planted panel (feature 134). orchestrator/_evaluate.py: evaluate_node runs execute → align → gate_targets → apply_costs → compute_node_metrics → marginal, then _persist writes the node row with a ScoreRecord carrying perturb_stability. NodeEvaluation carries fail_class and fail_detail. The architecture's fail_class vocabulary includes "tripwire_fail" (§ node schema). orchestrator/closeout.py: close_out splits evaluated nodes by root-mapped sidecar label (976633f, f3dca58) and persists KS, FDR, calibration and the discovery rate.

category.name: Tripwires in the Live Pipeline
category.feature: System declares the orchestrator member's dependency on the tripwires workspace member, so that `python -c "import orchestrator, tripwires"` returns without ImportError in a fresh `uv sync --all-packages` environment. - tripwires is added to packages/orchestrator/pyproject.toml dependencies and [tool.uv.sources] as a workspace source, and uv.lock is regenerated with `uv lock`. No other dependency changes.

System runs the six leakage tripwires on every evaluated node between metrics and the ledger debit, so that each node row returns its perturb_stability and a leaking node returns fail_class "tripwire_fail". - New module orchestrator._tripwire_step with run_tripwires(scores, targets, *, node_id), returning a frozen TripwireOutcome: - verdicts: the six verdict values, keyed by probe name - failed: the probe names that rejected, in a fixed order - perturb_stability: the lookback-jitter verdict's figure - axis_figures: the seed, window, subsample and lookback figures scores is the node's normalized per-date score panel (the vectors compute_node_metrics used). targets is the gated, post-cost target bundle at the metrics horizon: the same values the node is scored on, so null and real nodes are probed identically. Probe defaults are the tripwires member's own pinned DEFAULT_* constants, and nothing is configurable here. - evaluate_node calls it after compute_node_metrics and before the debit. A probe that raises a tripwires error (panel too thin, a series that never varied) is recorded as "not measured" for that probe and never fails the node: perturb_stability is None when the lookback probe could not measure, and the node proceeds. - When any probe rejects: - the node's fail_class is "tripwire_fail" - fail_detail names the failing probes and their figures - metrics are still persisted, so the evidence survives - the trial is still debited with the node's charges_budget - feature 131's poison is applied to the node and its subtree - When none rejects, the node is unchanged except that perturb_stability is written on its row and the four axis figures are recorded through stability.record_stability. - The node_evaluated event's score carries perturb_stability. - Wall time: run_tripwires over 92 dates × 40 symbols finishes in under 5 s on this host. Measure it in the test and assert under 15 s for slack under xdist. - test_tripwire_step.py: - A leak panel (scores equal to the target plus small noise) rejects on all six probes. - A seeded noise panel rejects on none. - A node through evaluate_node with an injected leaking executor ends with fail_class tripwire_fail, debited, row written and poisoned. A clean injected executor ends ok with a non-null perturb_stability. - A too-thin panel gives "not measured", not a failure. - Determinism: the same inputs give the same outcome. - A null node and a real node given identical panels produce identical outcomes.

System proves M1's tripwire exit on a sealed snapshot, so that the acceptance gate returns a failure if any tripwire stops catching a deliberately leaking signal. - tests/leakage/test_leaking_signal_caught.py builds a tmp sealed snapshot of daily bars (40 symbols, 120 days, seeded random walk) and evaluates through orchestrator.evaluate_node with a stub executor, never the real sandbox. Three cases: (a) a leaking signal whose score is the next day's return: every one of the six probes rejects, and the node is tripwire_fail (b) a lagged leak (the return two days ahead): it is still caught by at least the time-shuffle and label-permute probes (c) an honest 20-day momentum signal: no probe rejects, and perturb_stability is a finite number - The planted-leak corpus (tripwires.corpus) is run through run_tripwires and scores 0 escapes. - Runs in under 60 s and passes under pytest-xdist.

category.name: Triage on Real Campaigns
category.feature: System computes the M1 triage figure at close-out, so that `./run.sh closeout --campaign-id ID` returns the perturbation-stability AUC that separates the campaign's planted nulls from its real nodes. - close_out collects (perturb_stability, root-mapped label) for every evaluated node with a non-null perturb_stability, inside the process that already holds the sidecar. - It computes the AUC with real as the positive class and higher stability scoring as more real. This is a Mann–Whitney U / (n_real · n_null) with ties counted half. - CloseoutResult and the JSON line gain: - triage_auc: null when either side holds fewer than 2 nodes, never 0.5 by default - triage_null_count, triage_real_count - These are persisted in a new table closeout_triage (campaign_id PRIMARY KEY, auc, null_count, real_count, computed_at), created if absent and refreshed on rerun. - No node id or label is printed or stored. Only the three figures. - test_closeout_triage.py: - perfectly separated stabilities give AUC 1.0, and a reversed ordering gives 0.0 - ties give 0.5 - too few on one side gives triage_auc null and the rest of close-out unchanged - children are labelled by their root - a rerun refreshes the row It passes under pytest-xdist.
